questions.q: Name the components of blood.
questions.a: Plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

questions.q: What do platelets do?
questions.a: They help blood clot at wounds, stopping bleeding.

questions.q: Why is blood red?
questions.a: Haemoglobin, the red pigment in RBCs, carries oxygen and gives blood its colour.

solution_steps.name: beats_per_day
solution_steps.explain: the same rate extended to a full day

questions.q: A doctor counts 72 pulse beats in 1 minute... take 216 beats in 3 minutes. Find the pulse rate and beats per day.
questions.a: 103680 beats/min

questions.q: A pulse records 150 beats in 2 minutes. Calculate the pulse rate.
questions.a: 108000 beats/min

questions.q: An athlete at rest shows 168 beats in 3 minutes. Find the pulse rate and daily total.
questions.a: 80640 beats/min

questions.q: After running, 320 beats are counted in 4 minutes. What is the pulse rate?
questions.a: 115200 beats/min

questions.q: A pulse of 95 beats in 1 minute... take 190 beats in 2 minutes: find the rate.
questions.a: 136800 beats/min

concepts.title: Blood Vessels and Double Loop Circulation

questions.q: Name the three kinds of blood vessels.
questions.a: Arteries, veins and capillaries.

questions.q: Why do arteries have thick elastic walls?
questions.a: Blood leaves the heart at high pressure, so the walls must bear it.

questions.q: What is double circulation?
questions.a: Blood passes twice through the heart in one full trip - once to the lungs, once to the body.

concepts.title: Structure and Function of Human Heart

questions.q: Name the four chambers of the human heart.
questions.a: Left and right atria (upper) and left and right ventricles (lower).

questions.q: Which side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
questions.a: The right side - right atrium receives, right ventricle pumps to the lungs.

questions.q: Why are valves needed in the heart?
questions.a: They stop blood flowing backwards and keep it moving in one direction.

questions.q: What is a heartbeat?
questions.a: One complete contraction and relaxation of the heart that pushes blood into the vessels.

questions.q: How is the heartbeat related to the pulse?
questions.a: Each heartbeat sends a pressure wave along arteries, so the pulse rate at the wrist equals the heartbeats per minute.

questions.q: Which instrument records the heartbeat?
questions.a: A stethoscope (to hear it) and an ECG machine (to record its electrical pattern).

concepts.title: Human Excretory System and Urine Composition

solution_steps.name: urea_amount
solution_steps.explain: urine is about 2.5% urea by weight

questions.q: A person passes 1.2 L of urine in a day. How much urea does it carry, and how much water?
Daily urine output is 1.5 L. Calculate the urea in it and the water share.
Find the urea content of 0.8 L of urine and the water it holds.
A patient excretes 2 L of urine. What mass/volume of urea does that represent, and how much water?
With 1.1 L of urine passed, compute its urea and water parts.
What are the excretory organs of humans?
questions.a: The two kidneys (with urinary bladder and urethra); skin and lungs help too.

questions.q: What is urine made of?
questions.a: Mostly water with dissolved urea, salts and other wastes.

questions.q: Why must wastes like urea leave the body?
questions.a: They are poisonous if they build up, so kidneys filter them out with water as urine.

concepts.title: Transport of Water and Minerals via Xylem

questions.q: How does water rise in a plant against gravity?
questions.a: Root pressure pushes water up and transpiration pull from leaves draws the water column in xylem.

questions.q: What is xylem and what does it carry?
questions.a: Vascular tissue of tubes that carries water and minerals from roots to leaves.

questions.q: Why do plants need so much water?
questions.a: For photosynthesis, minerals transport, support (turgidity) and cooling by transpiration.

concepts.title: Transport of Synthesised Food via Phloem

questions.q: What does phloem transport?
questions.a: Food (sugar) made in leaves to all other parts - called translocation.

questions.q: In which direction does phloem carry food?
questions.a: Both up and down - wherever the plant needs food (roots, fruits, growing tips).

questions.q: Why is translocation necessary for plants?
questions.a: Every part needs food for energy and growth, but only leaves make it.

questions.q: What is transpiration?
questions.a: Loss of water vapour from leaves through stomata.

questions.q: How does transpiration help the plant?
questions.a: It pulls water up from roots, cools the plant, and keeps minerals flowing.

questions.q: When is transpiration fastest?
questions.a: On hot, dry, windy days when stomata are open.
